Position Description

About Harris County and Universal Services:

Harris County Universal Services is transforming the way the County does business and seeking a Director, Integrated Justice to join our team.

Universal Services is the enterprise IT solutions center for the departments and offices of Harris County, providing Information Technology, Public Safety and Justice Technologies, 311 Constituent Engagement Services, Fleet Services, and Records and Information Governance Services.

Harris County is the third largest and most diverse county in the nation, with a population of more than 4.7 million. Harris County Commissioners Court, the County’s governing body, directs a budget of more than $4 billion providing essential services including flood control, infrastructure, healthcare, housing, and justice administration.

This is a great time to join Universal Services as we enhance critical services to Harris County residents and internal customers.

The Director will be responsible for managing the day-to-day operations of the Integrated Justice (JWEB) application and for hiring and supervising the dedicated staff of the Integrated Justice Technology Division (IJTD) within the Universal Services Department (US). The IJTD Director will provide transparency into operations and project delivery of IJIS through regular reporting to the Integrated Justice Technology Committee Board of Directors. The position will be managed by IJTC Board and overseen administratively by the Chief Information Officer.

The IJTD Director brings a current knowledge and future vision of leveraging information and technology within a multifaceted program of information technology services for Harris County's justice, public safety, and court systems.

Ensures data integrity and system availability through proper approvals, maintenance, planning, and support.

Develops, manages, and tracks the IJIS annual budget.
Serves as the primary point of contact to the IJTC Board and key stakeholders while adhering to the existing US processes and standards for implementing and supporting applications.
Manages a team of IT professionals, including recruitment, training, and performance evaluation.
Maintains the highest ethical standards by consistently demonstrating honesty, integrity, respect, and confidentiality, while also adhering to Harris County and departmental policies and procedures.

You Belong Here

The Protiviti Career provides opportunity to learn, inspire, and advance within a collaborative and inclusive culture. We hire curious individuals for whom learning is a passion. We lean into our mission: We Care. We Collaborate. We Deliver.

Where We Need You: 

Protiviti is looking for a Technology Audit & Advisory Senior Manager to join our growing team.

What You Can Expect: 

As a Senior Manager, you’ll partner with our clients to manage risk associated with their use of technology. You'll develop strategies to solve complex business problems using new ways of thinking, and devise solutions to support your clients' needs through analytics, automation or the latest tools and methods.  You’ll develop lasting relationships with client personnel and further these relationships through quality product delivery.  You’ll foster a network within the business community and serve as an ambassador of Protiviti in the market. You will also be a mentor and provide performance development to teams as you oversee the successful completion of project work plans.

At Protiviti, Technology Audit & Advisory Focuses On

Helping clients better manage risks associated with their use of technology, protecting and enhancing enterprise value.
Innovation: identifying solutions to client problems related to technology, helping them to rethink how technology processes are managed by incorporating AI and automation.
Technology enablement: Incorporating analytics, AI, automation and other new tools and methods in the execution of audit work for our clients, enabling a deeper, broader, more efficient, and more insightful analysis of our clients’ technology risks.

Demonstrated experience with: 
Leading teams in implementing IT audit methodologies and developing necessary audit deliverables, including process flows, work programs, audit reports, and control summaries.   
Sarbanes-Oxley Act provisions and methodologies for achieving compliance, in particular the technology implications and requirements.

We are seeking an experienced IT Audit leader with deep technical expertise across cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, cloud infrastructure, and emerging technology risks.
This is a highly hands-on leadership position within a lean audit team. The successful candidate will lead complex technology audits from planning through reporting while remaining directly involved in technical testing and risk assessment. You will work closely with technology leaders, business stakeholders, audit professionals, and technical subject-matter experts.
The role requires someone who can operate at both the strategic and technical levels: developing audit strategies and emerging-risk perspectives while also understanding the underlying technology well enough to challenge technical teams and perform sophisticated audit procedures.
This is a hybrid position requiring at least three days per week in the office.

Key Responsibilities

Lead complex IT audits involving cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, cloud infrastructure, technology resiliency, systems architecture, and related emerging technologies.
Develop audit scopes, risk assessments, testing strategies, project plans, and reporting deliverables.
Perform hands-on technical audit testing across complex technology environments.
Identify significant technology risks and evaluate their potential business impact.
Participate in annual audit planning and help establish priorities around emerging technology and IT risks.
Lead walkthroughs, evaluate controls and processes, document conclusions, and develop clear audit findings and recommendations.
Present audit results and risk insights to management and technology stakeholders.
Develop perspectives and points of view on emerging areas such as AI, cybersecurity, cloud, and resiliency.
Manage audit projects while providing direction, coaching, and constructive feedback to other auditors.
Mentor team members and help strengthen their technical, analytical, and audit capabilities.
Build productive relationships with technology leaders and business partners.
Apply data analytics, automation, and AI tools to improve audit effectiveness and efficiency.
Identify innovative approaches to technical testing and help advance audit methodologies.
Stay current with rapidly evolving technologies, architectures, and associated risks.

Required Qualifications

At least 8 years of experience in IT Audit, IT Risk Management, or Information Security.
Significant hands-on experience auditing complex technology environments.
Deep technical expertise in one or more of the following: cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, cloud infrastructure, systems architecture, or information security.
Experience with cloud technologies such as Amazon Web Services.
Strong project management and audit leadership capabilities.
Previous experience coaching, mentoring, and providing feedback to audit professionals.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with highly technical audiences.
Strong critical-thinking and risk-assessment capabilities.
Experience developing and implementing data visualizations and analyzing complex datasets.
Experience with analytics and visualization tools such as Power BI, Tableau, Plotly, or Seaborn.

Experience applying AI solutions to improve audit execution and efficiency.
Demonstrated experience assessing AI solutions and associated risks.
Understanding of agentic AI architectures and their related risks.
Ability to learn and apply new technologies while assessing their associated risks and controls.

10+ years of experience in IT Audit, IT Risk Management, or Information Security.
5+ years of dedicated IT Audit experience.
Experience performing internal audit within a large, complex organization.
Experience in a Director or Manager-level IT Audit, infrastructure audit, cybersecurity audit, or related leadership position.

Master's degree or MBA in Computer Science, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, Mathematics, or a related discipline.

The Director of Technology Program Management (TPM) for Infrastructure Products & Services (Infrastructure) within the Global Product Organization (GPO) serves as a trusted advisor, partner, and source of leverage to the Infrastructure organization. They will resolve complex situations and manage multiple responsibilities simultaneously, appropriately prioritizing long-term projects with the urgency of immediate demands. new_jobs.description:
Sodali & Co is a recognized global capital markets stakeholder advisory firm, serving over 2,000 clients in more than 65 countries. The Firm advises a diverse and global client base including many of the world’s largest companies. Formed by the mergers of several market-leading capital markets stakeholder engagement consultancies, Sodali is the largest global shareholder services firm in the world. The Firm operates out of three global headquarters in New York, London, and Sydney and is supported by 12 regional offices in major financial capitals around the world.

Sodali provides a full suite of shareholder, sustainability, and strategic communications advisory services that, together, enable the Firm to deliver clients differentiated insights, integrated expertise, and bespoke advice to address complex interconnected issues, identify and capitalize on strategic opportunities, and drive successful business outcomes.

Sodali’s Services Include

Shareholder Advisory services include M&A Advisory, Activism Preparation and Defense, Board Governance Services, Corporate Governance Advisory, Proxy Solicitation, Capital Markets Intelligence, Global Debt and Bondholder Services, and Stakeholder Research.
Sustainability services include ESG Assessment, Strategy & Implementation, and Communications Advisory.
Strategic Communications services include Corporate Communications, Financial and Transaction Communications, Investor Relations, Public Affairs and Campaigns, Crisis and Special Situations, and Research.

The Opportunity

The Chief Technology Officer (CTO) will be a strategic leader in Sodali’s growth strategy. This individual will work with the Global Heads of our core practices, Finance, People, Business Operations, and Data Analytics to unite our technology strategy and our core business lines to drive real impact in our approach to data security, infrastructure, innovation, and data commercialization, and align technology initiatives with our business priorities. In this position, the CTO will be involved in matters related to agentic security, Snowflake administration, Azure deployment, cloud services, RFP management and ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type 2 audits. This role will lead the IT help desk team and office infrastructure teams globally.

This position is located in New York. Relocation assistance is not available for this position.

Key Responsibilities

Implement best-in-class IT operations and infrastructure across the firm globally. This includes updating systems, cybersecurity, and setting global IT policies.
Lead digital transformation, update infrastructure, strengthen cybersecurity, and enabling scalable systems that support Sodali’s worldwide footprint
Drive security governance standards, including remaining aware of any regional shifts in compliance or security standards.
Lead global IT improvement projects while adhering to regional compliance requirements.
Improve resiliency and efficiency of current systems and infrastructure.
Deploy Azure and cloud services with an eye for streamlining processes and procedures
Coordinate with internal stakeholders regarding .
Align technology strategy with overall business priorities, including staying agile as priorities expand with a high-growth organization.
Champion innovation and emerging technology adoption — including AI and agentic systems — to create competitive advantage for the Firm.
Partner with Data Analytics and practice leaders to identify and develop opportunities to commercialize Sodali’s proprietary data assets.

Qualifications

12+ years of information technology experience, preferably in a high-growth, finance or professional-services environment.
Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Technology, or a related field. Relevant certifications such as CISSP, PMP, or ITIL are preferred.
Strong experience managing a Microsoft environment.
Salesforce, NetSuite, and Snowflake Administration experience.
Experience managing GPU infrastructure for LLM training and inference preferred.
Proven success in developing and executing global, integrated strategies.
Experience driving innovation programs and identifying data monetization or commercialization opportunities preferred.
Experience managing integrations of mergers and acquisitions.
Strong experience partnering with advisory and executive leadership teams.
Track record of leading organizations through change, transformation, or scale.
Strategic and creative, with a strong focus on execution.
Exceptional communication and presentation skills; credible and influential at the executive level.
Comfort working in fast-paced, evolving environments where priorities may shift.
Proactive, self-starter, comfortable working in a flat organization.

new_jobs.title: Fractional Chief Information Officer
new_jobs.description:
Rare is a global leader in community-led conservation. For more than 50 years, we have partnered with local communities worldwide to strengthen their stewardship of the lands and waters they depend on.

Today, Rare works in some of the world’s most biodiverse places, where climate risks are high and community-led conservation can deliver the greatest impact. We combine community-driven solutions with behavioral science, partnerships, financing, and practical innovation to create the conditions for conservation to succeed. By helping make local leadership the foundation of conservation, we strengthen resilience for people and nature.

As Rare seeks to scale these critically needed and effective conservation solutions, the organization is committed to modernizing our use of technology scale. The Fractional CIO will lead Rare’s transition from fragmented, locally managed systems to an integrated technology and operating environment built for intelligence at scale. This work will modernize the systems that underpin Rare’s work delivering impact to hundreds of thousands of people in dozens of countries. To achieve this transition, the role will concentrate on implementing Rare’s FY27 priorities:

Building and rolling out Salesforce for grants management
Selecting and implementing a global HRIS
Providing strategic guidance for Rare’s org-wide Microsoft 365 rollout, already underway
Guiding Rare’s Automation and Applied AI strategy

We are looking for a senior technology leader to drive key systems efforts while putting in place the governance and internal capacities needed for the long term. This is a delivery role, not an advisory one. You will own outcomes, manage implementation partners, and make architecture and investment decisions.

Reporting to the Senior Vice President of Strategy and Organizational Development, you will be supported by a cross-functional team with clear, complementary roles:

Rare’s Vice President of Technology:
and Rare’s Technology team will serve as the primary technical partner and will ensure alignment with Rare’s broader technology environment.
The Vice President of Learning and Development:
will lead change management and staff adoption.
The Director of Systems and Special Projects:
will bring knowledge of Rare’s systems and drive project management.
Leaders from Finance, Talent, Development, and Programs:
will guide process decisions and champion adoption within their teams. External implementation partners will bring specialized expertise and additional delivery capacity.
External implementation partners for Salesforce and a HRIS will bring specialized expertise and additional delivery capacity.

Expected Outcomes of the Engagement

Salesforce grants management designed, built, and rolling out.
Establish a consistent, transparent process from funding opportunity through grant closeout, delivered in phases in partnership with Development, Finance, and Programs. You will select and manage the implementation partner, ensuring high-quality delivery and value for money.
A global HRIS selected, contracted, and moving into implementation.
Lead requirements gathering, vendor selection, contracting, and implementation planning in partnership with Talent and other business owners, leaving Rare with a well-governed program underway.
Microsoft 365 strategically guided, not directly led.
The rollout is already underway and will remain with the internal project team. Your role will be to provide strategic guidance on governance, integration, and alignment with Rare’s broader technology architecture.

To support the implementation of these systems and sustain them over time, you will:

Establish clear decision rights and named owners for core platforms, data, integrations, security, vendors, and technology investments.
Define a coherent technology architecture, including standards for access, privacy, security, and business continuity, as well as authoritative sources for priority organizational data.
Recommend a technology operating model that identifies the leadership, staffing, capabilities, and external support Rare will need after the fractional engagement concludes.
Develop a short, prioritized set of automation and AI opportunities, with clear recommendations about where Rare should invest, scale, adapt, or stop.

Primary Responsibilities

Deliver Priority Systems

Lead Salesforce grants management design, implementation, and phased rollout, including selecting and managing the implementation partner ,
in partnership with Development, Finance, and Programs.
Guide HRIS requirements, vendor selection, contracting, implementation planning, and initial rollout in partnership with Talent and other business owners.
Hire and oversee implementation consultants for Salesforce and HRIS, ensuring delivery quality and value for money.
Provide light strategic guidance to the internal team leading Microsoft 365 migration and adoption.
Work with business owners to simplify and standardize priority processes before configuring technology around them.

Establish Governance and Integration

Develop and maintain technology governance practices in partnership with the Vice President of Technology, ensuring governance decisions are grounded in Rare’s existing environment.
Define platform ownership, product ownership, decision rights, data stewardship, and accountability across enterprise, regional, and country levels.
Establish lightweight governance for architecture, integrations, data, security, privacy, access, vendors, and technology investments.
Define how core platforms connect and which systems serve as authoritative sources for priority organizational data.
Incorporate cybersecurity, compliance, business continuity, and risk management into system and vendor decisions.

Enable Adoption and Internal Ownership

Partner with the Vice President of Learning and Development, who will lead change management, to ensure communication, staff engagement, and role-based support are built into each implementation.
Work closely with the Vice President of Technology and Technology team to align new platforms with Rare’s existing infrastructure, security, and support model.
Recommend a sustainable technology operating model and identify internal technology skills needed for Rare following the fractional engagement.

Guide Automation and Applied AI

Identify a small number of practical opportunities for automation and AI to improve staff effectiveness, organizational decision-making, or program delivery.
Align AI investments with Rare’s technology architecture, information governance, security, and change management approach.

Future Priorities

After gaining traction on the delivery of the FY27 priorities, assess Rare’s current technology strategy and present recommendations for the next phase of strategic priorities, investments, and implementation.

Experience and Qualifications

Over 10 years of senior technology leadership experience as a CIO, CTO, technology transformation leader, or equivalent advisor.
Demonstrated success leading enterprise systems modernization from strategy and architecture through implementation, adoption, and benefits realization.
Experience with Salesforce-based business platforms and HRIS selection and implementation.
Working knowledge of Microsoft 365 and SharePoint, system integration, enterprise data governance, cybersecurity, privacy, identity and access management, vendor management, and technology risk.
Experience coordinating internal teams, business owners, consultants, and vendors across multiple initiatives.
Experience working in a globally distributed or federated organization; nonprofit, international development, or conservation experience is helpful but not required.
Practical understanding of responsible AI and automation, including how to assess potential value, risks, and organizational readiness.

Leadership Approach

The successful candidate will be:
Strategic and hands-on, able to move between executive decisions and implementation detail.
Enterprise-minded while grounded in the needs of staff, programs, regions, and country teams.
Decisive and pragmatic, with the judgment to simplify, sequence, and stop work when evidence warrants it.
Effective at delivering results through cross-functional teams rather than relying on direct authority.
Committed to responsible, secure, inclusive, and sustainable uses of technology.
Impact oriented with a passion for Rare’s mission and the people we serve.

Time Commitment

The role will be 15-20 hours per week over the course of 11 months: November 2026 through September 2027.

How to Respond

Interested candidates should submit a résumé and a brief letter of interest (no more than one page) outlining:
Relevant experience leading comparable systems modernization efforts, particularly Salesforce and HRIS implementations, with examples of engagements and results achieved.
Availability from November 2026 through September 2027, including the ability to commit approximately 15–20 hours per week.
Proposed fees on an hourly, monthly, or engagement basis.

Please also provide names and contact information for two professional references.

Candidates responding on behalf of a firm should identify the individual who would serve as Fractional CIO and describe the roles of any additional team members.

Please send application materials to Renee Baiorunos at rbaiorunos@rare.org by October 23, 2026
. Selected candidates will be invited to discuss their experience, proposed approach, and fit with Rare’s cross-functional team.
